books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: General Robert E. Lee, General Order No. 9 (April 10, 1865)

stimulus.source_note: General Robert E. Lee, General Order No. 9, April 10, 1865. Public domain. “. . .” marks omitted text.
stimulus.text:
“After four years of arduous service marked by unsurpassed courage and fortitude, the Army of Northern Virginia has been compelled to yield to overwhelming numbers and resources. . . . I need not tell the survivors of so many hard-fought battles, who have remained steadfast to the last, that I have consented to the result from no distrust of them.”

—General Robert E. Lee, General Order No. 9 (Farewell Address), April 10, 1865

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Lee tells his men he consented to surrender “from no distrust of them.” His purpose in saying this was most likely to

options.text: blame his men for losing the war.
options.misconception: Saying he does not distrust them is the opposite of blaming them.

options.text: urge his men to keep fighting.
options.misconception: Lee has already surrendered; the address is a farewell, not a call to arms.
Lee praises his own men’s courage; he does not praise the Union army here.

options.text: preserve his soldiers’ honor in defeat.

rationales.A: Saying he does not distrust them is the opposite of blaming them.
rationales.B: Lee has already surrendered; the address is a farewell, not a call to arms.
rationales.C: Lee praises his own men’s courage; he does not praise the Union army here.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Lee’s men had fought for four years, and Lee wanted their service remembered with honor.
rationales.general:
1. A surrender can look like a judgment on the soldiers who fought it.
2. Lee removes that reading in advance: he did not surrender because he distrusted them.
3. He has already praised their courage and fortitude in the same address.
4. Background from the books: Lee’s men had fought for four years, and Lee wanted their service remembered with honor.
Remember: a farewell that clears the soldiers of blame is guarding their honor.
